id: E-d mechanism (revised): the keel's upkeep is drawn from the living's memories of their dead, found by the names entered on a roll; names kept, faces lost
resembles: Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind (Lacuna: clients bring in every object tied to one person, the clinic uses them to locate the memories and erase them; same shape for the procedure)
Yoko Ogawa, The Memory Police (whole island loses a category from memory at once, the words and objects remain and nobody can place them; same shape for the cost's texture)
Garcia Marquez, One Hundred Years of Solitude (the insomnia plague: Macondo labels everything because the labels outlast the meaning; same shape for the cost's texture)
Lowry, The Giver (when the Receiver leaves, the memory burden one person held goes back to the whole community; same shape for the burden moving off one person)
Ishiguro, The Buried Giant (communal forgetting buys survival; same shape for the cost, already in the plan)
medieval mortuary rolls and chantry rolls (households give names of their dead to a clerk to be entered and prayed for: a real custom, the queue's nearest source)
why: No work I can recall uses this mechanism: a deliberate, public, ongoing payment in which a written name is the address and the memory it points to is what is spent. Each close work has one part of it. Eternal Sunshine is the nearest on procedure (bring a cue for one person, the memory is found by it and removed), but it is private, a relief, and undone by love. The Memory Police and Macondo are the nearest on what the town lives with afterwards (the record stays, the meaning goes, from everyone at once), but there it happens to them, as an affliction, and is not a price. The Giver is the nearest on structure (a burden one person carried passes to everyone), and the plan already names it. None combines consent, the name as address and the split of names kept from faces lost.
fix: Add The Memory Police and One Hundred Years of Solitude to Nearest works, since a literary reader will think of them at B52's unplaceable name. Keep the B51 queue to names only: nobody brings keepsakes, photographs or objects, which is Lacuna's waiting room with its bag of things.

id: E-d mechanism: the other named works
resembles: Coco (the second death; the photo carries the face, the reverse split)
Le Guin, Earthsea (true names; the dry land's dead forget the living)
Pathologic 1-2 (a town bound to a dying ground, ritual over the dead; nothing about memory spent by name)

Planescape: Torment (Dhall, the Dustman scribe who writes every dead arrival's name in the Mortuary's ledger; with the amnesiac immortal and B49's past-self record it adds to an existing Torment pile)
Sunless Sea / Fallen London (memories as a currency, Mr Eaten's erased name)
Pratchett: Death's hourglasses with names; Going Postal's GNU keeping dead names in motion
Memento (the written record outlasting memory; already a rejected alternative)
Black Mirror, The Entire History of You and Crocodile (recorded memory, recall forced on others)
Spiritfarer (ferrying and letting go of the dead)
Death Note (a name in a book, plus knowing the face; a joke reader may connect 'names kept, faces lost' to it)
Spirited Away, Your Name, Natsume's Book of Friends (names taken, names forgotten, a book of names as handles)
NieR Replicant ending D, Madoka (a person erased from everyone's memory)
why: Each shares one ingredient (names, the dead, memory as currency, a written record) and none uses consent-given memory of the dead as payment with the name kept. The Wandering Inn I can't recall a close scene in, so I make no claim there. The only one worth watching is Torment: Dhall's ledger plus the amnesiac immortal returning from death plus B49's record of a past self make a cluster, though each part is generic on its own.

id: First check, B49: the failed design must fail by cascade, not headcount
resembles: Planescape: Torment, Outer Wilds, Returnal (the record of a past failed attempt; named honestly in the plan now)
why: Fixed in the beat, not just the mapping: no count, no date, no note in your hand; the ticks are crossed first in one stroke, then all the rest in one long one; turn down; B12's matching count is cut and E-d has no population gate. The cascade itself is well planted, better than §4 says: kin-link cascades are a combat mechanic from B23 (day 31, 'the first cascade through a pack'), hollowed clerks drop a whole street at once, and B42 shows the Breaking as a cascade. So a reader can complete 'one went and it took them all' and see that more sharers make it worse.
fix: In §4's 'Sharing among the living fails' row, list B23 (31) and B42 (64) as plants. They are the ones doing the work, and listing them means phase 2 keeps them.

id: First check, B11: no physical effect before SB-face
why: Fixed in the beat: the sitting-up, the burning at first light, an unnamed mark on the tally board; 'No physical effect, and the camp's stone is not used.' B21 and B27 are custom only. The first physical effect is SB-face (~55).

id: First check: the dead off the respawn stone; 'the Kindling'
resembles: Dark Souls (Fire Keepers; bonfires; the kindling vocabulary)
why: Fixed: no body touches any stone, the climax is a clerk's table, and Kindling is gone. What is left is that the Hearth is still the stone you come back to, and it is now paid for by the town's remembrance of its dead. That is far from a bonfire built on bones and fed Humanity. A smaller word cluster remains: ash, 'kept', the creatures called Keepers (Dark Souls' Fire Keepers tend the bonfires), and a warm stone you return to. Each word is plain; together they are a soft echo, not a borrowing.
fix: Optional, for the renaming branch: give the Keeper creature a different plain word (they file you, so a clerical one fits). Not a blocker.

id: First check, B44: no staging; N6's reason on the page
why: Fixed: 'Nothing is laid out or pointed at'. N6's reason is in his own margin at B39 ('requires the leave of every household; not obtainable'), so 'I have no other way' is sincere rather than a lie or a nudge. The stance is sane and turns out wrong, which the first check asked for.

id: §4 C-promise-17 and B39: the answer is written out at day 59, not first made the answer at B49
why: B39 shows a costing that prices the upkeep from 'remembrance of the deceased', with the precondition beside it ('the leave of every household'). After B27 and SB-face, that is the whole of E-d, in writing, at day 59. §4 says the mechanism 'only at B49 (76)' becomes the answer, which understates it. 19 days before B50 is inside the plan's own 40-day rule, so this is not solved too early, but the answer still arrives as a found document, the convenience the first check noted (moved from B49 to B39, from your hand to the enemy's).
fix: Correct §4: earliest fair guess at B39 (59). Optionally make B39's line less complete: price the line and strike it, *supply irregular*, and leave N6's 'requires the leave of every household' for B44, said aloud as the reason he has no other way. Then the precondition, which is what the town supplies, comes as a person's words at the moment the question is posed, not from a document.

id: §1 rule 'a draw on the living cascades': why doesn't the anchor's own forgetting cascade into the town?
why: As written, any working that draws from one living mind runs along its shared-history links to everyone it shares a life with. But every Black Drift has drawn the anchor's whole memory, including its memories of town 1's to town 4's people (N9 among them), and those towns did not forget; they fell apart and left. Under E-d a short reserve takes 'some of the player's memory' from an anchor who now knows the whole town. E-c's N3 forgets daily. A sharp reader who has just used B49 to rule out sharing will ask why the same rule leaves the anchor alone, and the plan has no answer. This is the logic the ending stands on.
fix: Make the plants already in the plan carry it: the Chequer seal on a holder's wrist closes the holder's links to a working's draw, which is why the registry selected *present, no dependants* and why the cascade stopped at the sealed anchor every time. Town 3's sharers had no seals (the B49 ring's small circles carry no seal mark), so the draw ran through them. N3 is sealed too. One line in world.md; no new beat. B25's charcoal copy that works once becomes a hint that a seal is a mechanism, not a badge.

id: B27 / B35: the Warm say names aloud and keep them, but §1 says the name survives the draw because it is written
why: §1: 'What is written is not sense in a mind, so the draw leaves it.' That implies an unwritten name would be taken along with the face. But at B27 the Warm speak their lists of names into the crack and can still give every name, and at B35 the elder says the porter's wife's name aloud and he keeps it (he still knows whose face he has lost). So either speaking is enough and the roll is only leave and bookkeeping, or the Warm's names contradict the rule. A reader putting E-d together from B27 and B35 will build the wrong rule, or catch the contradiction.
fix: Write the names at the plants too: the Warm read their names off the crack's lip, where generations of them are scratched into the rock, and at B35 the elder scratches the wife's name there before saying it. That plants the roll at day 38 with no added line of explanation.

id: B51 / §5 factions: 'requires the leave of every household', and the Hall resists E-d
why: If E-d needs every household, then either the Hall gives in off-page or the queue is unanimous, and a whole town queuing as one, consenting to the precondition the Chequer called unobtainable, is the tidy irony the first check warned about, now made into the climax. The plan states the Hall resists but never says what that resistance costs or changes.
fix: Make the leave per name, not per town: each household gives leave for its own dead. Households that refuse keep their dead's faces, the roll is shorter, the reserve thinner, and the Hall's resistance shows in the S-names strand and in who isn't in the queue. Drop 'every household' from N6's margin note or keep it as his mistaken premise (he assumed it had to be all or nothing).

id: §1 'A dead person holds no sense' against world.md's Taking ('a human carries more weight (sense) than any animal', fast in things that ate the dead)
why: world.md says a dead human body still carries sense; that is why eating a thing that ate a man is dangerous. 'A link to them has no far end' is only true once the body is spent. The plan keeps the burning, so the fix is already there, but the rule as worded contradicts canon, and phase 2 will copy the wording into world.md.
fix: Word the rule through the fire: the burned dead have no far end (fire spends the leftover, per the Taking). The sitting-up and burning at B11, B21 and B27 then plant the rule as well as the custom, and an unburned body becomes a hazard to the draw, which the Wall's carrying the dead home after B51 already implies.

why: Most players won't know the word, so they will read it by its parts, and the parts are 'ass' and 'art'. As a capitalised proper noun at the head of the world's founding catastrophe it will be read that way, said that way and memed (the Dark Souls community's 'try finger but hole' is the model). The register is dry and dark, and a crude joke on the most solemn word in the canon is a constant leak. The fallback has the same etymology (assart comes from Anglo-French essart), the same Exchequer link, and nothing to snag on. It reads as foreign and archaic, which suits a Chequer term.
fix: Use 'the Essart'. Keep the in-fiction gloss through context (cleared, burned ground; its rents on the Chequer's books) and never define it in player text. If the lead wants a native word instead, 'the Ridding' (cleared land; place-name Riddings) is plain and carries 'riddance', but that is the lead's call.
